clue.text: What's fair, square and superior to sawn timber?

parts.note: above means higher than or superior to
a board is a plank of sawn timber

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what is honest and also sits on top of a plank.
explanation.definitionFit: Both fair and square describe honest, open dealing with nothing concealed.

clue.text: One whose wine-bibbing guest might be expected to be late

definitions.text: One whose wine-bibbing guest might be expected to be late

parts.words: One whose wine-bibbing guest might be expected to be late
parts.note: late means dead: the Renaissance family notorious for poisoning dinner guests

explanation.walkthrough: 'late' is not tardy but deceased: Lucrezia and Cesare were reputed to poison guests' wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance Italian family was infamous for poisoning rivals at the table.

clue.text: Bad upset in material that's potentially invalid.

indicators.note: in says the turned word sits inside the fabric

parts.note: voile is a thin, sheer fabric

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word over, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Faulty fabric overturned and declared possibly null.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses BAD to DAB, and 'in' puts it inside VOILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract that can be annulled is capable of being made null.

clue.text: Waylay. Rose perhaps?

definitions.meaning: to accost and detain someone for a talk
a flower worn in the lapel slit, an example rather than a definition

explanation.surface: Ambush someone, or wear a rose on your lapel.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttonhole is to detain someone in talk; a lapel flower is called by the same name.

clue.text: Bill's story

definitions.meaning: an invoice of charges
a narrative report

explanation.surface: A man named Bill tells his tale.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice and a narrative report share this word.

clue.text: Takes note of lodgings

definitions.meaning: slang for understands or appreciates, as in 'I dig it'
rented rooms, British informal

explanation.walkthrough: Digs is British slang for rented rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for appreciates or understands; also British informal for rented rooms.

clue.text: Delightful-if not amorous with everybody ?

definitions.meaning: lovely, charming
someone who is fond of a few people rather than all

explanation.surface: Charming, unless you are fond of all and sundry.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into two: one who loves a few, not everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word means lovable or charming; split, it is someone fond of a few rather than all.

clue.text: Agenda — make sure 'of your Times !

definitions.meaning: a parliamentary list of the day's business
reserve your copy of the newspaper with the newsagent

explanation.surface: A reminder from the newspaper to reserve a copy.
explanation.walkthrough: An order paper lists Parliament's daily business; separately, you order a paper such as The Times from the newsagent.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament's daily schedule of business; also reserving your newspaper at the shop.

clue.text: In such 'games the sky is not the limit.

definitions.text: In such 'games the sky is not the limit.

parts.words: In such 'games the sky is not the limit.
parts.note: games played under a roof have a ceiling, not the open sky, as their upper boundary

explanation.walkthrough: 'The sky's the limit' means no upper bound; under a roof the ceiling is the limit instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports played inside a building have a roof above them rather than open air.

clue.text: Blithe Spirit's profuse strains were unpremeditatedly so

definitions.text: Blithe Spirit's profuse strains were unpremeditatedly so

parts.words: Blithe Spirit's profuse strains were unpremeditatedly so
parts.note: Shelley's skylark pours its heart 'in profuse strains of unpremeditated art', so its song was spontaneously creative

explanation.walkthrough: Blithe Spirit looks like the Noel Coward play, but this is Shelley's poem To a Skylark, whose bird sings 'in profuse strains of unpremeditated art'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpremeditated art is creativity of a natural, aesthetic kind.

clue.text: No longer 'used to be worried about fish

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the shuffled pair is placed round the fish
worried letters are shaken up, so the two short words are rearranged

parts.note: a sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: Something no longer in use that once caused anxiety about fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' turns TO BE into OBTE, and 'about' wraps those letters round SOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outdated has fallen out of service and been superseded.

clue.text: Writer Charles, or his sister's'follower ?

definitions.meaning: Charles ..., the English essayist who wrote as Elia
his sister was Mary, and in the nursery rhyme Mary had a little one that followed her to school

explanation.surface: A question about the essayist and his sister's companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb's sister was Mary Lamb; the nursery rhyme 'Mary had a little lamb' has the animal follow her everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb was the essayist; the rhyme's young sheep trailed after Mary.

clue.text: Alas — to. have 'no flower!

definitions.meaning: an old exclamation of regret
to be without a particular bloom, split into three words

explanation.walkthrough: Lackadaisy is an old variant of lackaday, a cry of sorrow; split up it says to be without a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic exclamation of sorrow; split, it means being without a meadow bloom.

clue.text: A fool in company with a parliamentarian gets in no work

indicators.note: gets in says the run before it goes inside the following word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
MP stands for Member of Parliament
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: An idiot who keeps company with an MP and never does any work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in' puts INCOMP inside NO, giving NINCOMPO, and OP follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A nincompoop is a silly, foolish person; simpleton is a synonym.

clue.text: Danish wassail ".custom would be less, honoured in this

definitions.text: Danish wassail ".custom would be less, honoured in this

parts.words: Danish wassail ".custom would be less, honoured in this
parts.note: Hamlet calls Danish drinking 'a custom more honour'd in the breach than the' keeping

explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet says the Danish carousing is 'a custom more honour'd in the breach than the observance': more honoured in breaking, so less honoured in keeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a custom is the act of following or honouring it.

clue.text: Plain refugee came first to a city of knights

indicators.note: first places the word came ahead of the refugee

parts.note: taken as written
Lot fled Sodom, one of the biblical cities of the plain

explanation.surface: A displaced person from the plains arrives at a knightly city.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Lot escapes the destruction of the cities of the plain, so he is the 'Plain refugee'.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's court and its Round Table knights were based at this legendary city.

clue.text: Relevant stuff

definitions.meaning: pertinent, as in ... evidence
fabric or substance

explanation.definitionFit: Pertinent evidence, or fabric and substance in general.

clue.text: Ignition first-afterwards this pile-up

parts.note: burning leaves cinders first, and afterwards they are gathered into a mound of refuse

explanation.walkthrough: Read in two halves: what ignition leaves comes first, and a pile follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A dump of cinders and refuse is the mound left after fires are cleared.

clue.text: Instrument with which William gets the bird

parts.note: a horn is a brass instrument
Bill is a pet form of William

explanation.surface: William plays an instrument and gets booed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets the bird' sounds like being jeered, but the bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical species with a huge casqued beak.

clue.text: Maybe thus' win a holiday

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Perhaps this is how to win a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' rearranges THUS and WIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Whit Sunday, Pentecost, was traditionally a British bank holiday.

clue.text: The natural state? Entirely.

definitions.meaning: naked, the state nature made us
wholly or completely

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the altogether' is an idiom for being nude.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in the altogether' means nude, and the adverb means completely.

clue.text: Bring up the back

definitions.meaning: to raise children or animals
the hindmost part

explanation.surface: An instruction to follow at the very end of a column.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear is to raise young; the rear is the hind part.

clue.text: Where Arthur 'finally barged in?

parts.note: the dying king was carried away on a barge to his last resting place

explanation.walkthrough: 'barged in' seems to mean intruded, but the wounded King Arthur was taken by barge to the isle where legend says he rests.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary isle where King Arthur was borne after his last battle.

clue.text: Unduly proud of skill which includes organ repair

indicators.note: which includes means the skill word holds the rest inside it

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation

indicators.note: repair means the letters of the instrument are mended into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone too proud of their talent for mending organs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair' turns ORGAN into ROGAN, and 'which includes' puts that inside ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Being haughty means having an inflated opinion of one's own worth.

clue.text: A swelling-up afresh

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a wen is a cyst or swelling on the skin

explanation.surface: A lump growing up once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses WEN to NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting again means doing it over a second time.

clue.text: Art thou not, fatal vision, — To feeling as to sight?" (Macbeth)

definitions.text: Art thou not, fatal vision, — To feeling as to sight?" (Macbeth)

parts.words: Art thou not, fatal vision, — To feeling as to sight?" (Macbeth)
parts.note: the dagger speech, with the missing word before 'To feeling' meaning perceptible to the senses

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is Macbeth's dagger soliloquy: 'Art thou not, fatal vision, sensible / To feeling as to sight?' The gap is the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's usage the word means able to be perceived by the senses.

clue.text: Wrap things up — blow the Governor !

parts.note: a swat is a sharp blow
HE, His Excellency, is the title of a colonial governor

explanation.surface: An impatient order to finish up and strike the man in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for His Excellency, the style of a governor or ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: To swaddle or bind round is to wrap something in bandages or cloth.

clue.text: Amazing place at the end of a rabbit-hole

definitions.text: Amazing place at the end of a rabbit-hole

parts.words: Amazing place at the end of a rabbit-hole
parts.note: Alice follows the White Rabbit down its burrow into Lewis Carroll's realm of marvels

explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll's Alice tumbles down a rabbit-hole into a land of marvels.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's realm where Alice has her adventures is a place full of marvels.
